name: Killer Queen live win probability predictor

mentions.name: Killer Queen live win probability predictor
mentions.description: This project is a live win probability predictor for the 10-player arcade game Killer Queen, predicting the winner causally, event by event. It compares a nanoGPT-based model that treats events as tokens (about 65% accuracy) against a LightGBM baseline trained on hand-engineered expert features (about 70% accuracy), and is moving to a hybrid approach that feeds expert features back in as additional tokens or auxiliary loss heads and uses the LightGBM model as a teacher for knowledge distillation. It generates personalized post-game feedback by tracking sharp swings in win probability (ΔWP) to automatically produce highlight and lowlight reels right after a match, and uses ΔWP as a heuristic to identify match turning points for automated YouTube summaries.
mentions.problem: Identifying the exact moments where plays were effective or catastrophic requires manually scrubbing through hours of Twitch footage; on the modeling side, the transformer approach trails a LightGBM baseline by 5% accuracy despite being roughly 4 orders of magnitude more expensive to train.
mentions.audience: Players of the 10-player arcade game Killer Queen, plus content creators summarizing matches for YouTube
mentions.source_excerpt: I’ve been experimenting with a live win probability predictor for the 10-player arcade game Killer Queen. The goal is to predict the winner in a causal, event-by-event fashion.
